searchText: In slot 93504, I submitted a heavy but invalid payload and it looks like the ELs stalled for 8 slots right after with all payloads being missing. Prysm-nethermind forked off again, like yesterday (missed a proposal) but eventually recovered. Someone having the logs of prysm-nethermind-1? cc <@412614104222531604> ~~Also, I think my payload also DoS'd <@&1070471163219824730> , which would point to a missing early-abort check.~~ edit: reth might be fine actually. In slot 93504, I submitted a heavy but I'm running local devnets, 12 nodes, 128 validators each, spammoor active, limits at 21 blobs, and I see lighthouse constantly trying to reorg payloads and its blocks being reorged. This can be anything so don't try to diagnose it, I'm running with hacked up clients and I'm not sure if I'm causing this or LH is just behaving incorrectly, could be peering, could be bad voting, etc. But have you guys been testing under constant load and self building with about 21 blobs constantly? without heavy blob count my local devnets work fine, no problem can you share your kurtosis setup? you're not going to like it as I am running a hidden image for one of the nodes. happy to wait no worries 😂 that's the conf All three clients eventually go to crap with that haven't tried the same config with LH + PRysm + Any other vanilla client on this laptop We are sending blobs on plataberget, I can try a short burst, filling up blocks completely 🙂 But we avoid spamming blobs too heavily as it eats disk space pretty fast (all our nodes are supernodes due to the validator count). tbh, a 12 pairs devnet (24 clients) with full blob spamming sounds like a lot for a local laptop 😆 nah if this is breaking on kurtosis is probably better to test like that very cheaply <@808969530608451584> , copying from tthe steel channel: ah yeah this is with local block building, that's important unless the builder is also not well peered anyway, it may be just my local setup which is pretty ad-hoc so don't worry much about this, I just noticed that both Prysm and LH fuck up after about 500 slots of a constant backlog of blobs I think it's because the ELs mempool protection starts to pick up and then getBlobs fails and you can't recover from the EL I believ you guys are not testing these paths if the ELs are really spammed with different blob transactions AND we locally build, then each builder will have a different mempool view and therefore the blobs that are sent are not going to be covered by all ELs and local recovery fails this is one way of actually testing column broadcast if OTOH you use always the same builder like buildoor then that mempool is draining constantly Let me copy this in #interop, perhaps some cl-dev also tests locally

<@808969530608451584> , copying from tthe steel channel:
ah yeah this is with local block building, that's important unless the builder is also not well peered
anyway, it may be just my local setup which is pretty ad-hoc
so don't worry much about this, I just noticed that both Prysm and LH fuck up after about 500 slots
of a constant backlog of blobs
I think it's because the ELs mempool protection starts to pick up and then getBlobs fails
and you can't recover from the EL
I believ you guys are not testing these paths
if the ELs are really spammed with different blob transactions AND we locally build, then each builder will have a different mempool view
and therefore the blobs that are sent are not going to be covered by all ELs and local recovery fails
this is one way of actually testing column broadcast
if OTOH you use always the same builder like buildoor then that mempool is draining constantly
Let me copy this in #interop, perhaps some cl-dev also tests locally
